summary.headline: Cyient Q1 FY27: DET revenue $162.5M, down 0.5% QoQ in constant currency, while DET EBIT margin rose to 13.2% and the 15% target slipped to H1 FY28.
summary.overview: DET revenue was flat-to-down in constant currency (-0.5% QoQ, -0.9% YoY) but rose 2.7% QoQ and 10.6% YoY in rupee terms. Normalized DET EBIT margin expanded to 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ, +114 bps YoY) on cost optimisation and a stronger USD. Management pushed out its 15% EBIT target from Q4 FY27 to around H1 FY28 because revenue ramp-up is lagging, and it said mid-single-digit FY27 growth is now hard to achieve. Group revenue was $219M (+4.5% QoQ, +9.1% YoY in constant currency), with Kinetic Technologies consolidated for the first time.

segments.name: DET (Digital Engineering & Technology)
segments.commentary: Revenue $162.5M, -0.5% QoQ cc, with normalized EBIT margin of 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ). Transportation & mobility grew 3% QoQ and 14.8% YoY cc, while strategic units fell 8.2% QoQ on energy weakness.

segments.name: Cyient DLM
segments.commentary: Management said the quarter closed with its highest-ever order book and book-to-bill above 1.5, with double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters. No DLM financial figures were given on the call.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Combined revenue $17.9M including Kinetic ($10.4M). Organic business $7.5M (+5% QoQ). Management expects breakeven only in FY28, with about $3M per quarter of Kinetic-related amortisation to cover.

guidance_outlook: 15% DET EBIT target now expected about H1 FY28 rather than Q4 FY27, because revenue ramp-up is behind plan while cost levers are on track.
No formal revenue guidance; management said mid-single-digit growth for FY27 will be challenged and it is 'hopeful' of meaningful growth returning in H2 FY27.
Full-year DET effective tax rate expected at 27-28%.
Semiconductor breakeven expected in FY28; high-voltage/high-power ASSP development to consume cash for at least the next four to five quarters.
TAO Digital Solutions closing expected by August 2026 (late Q2); TAO revenue expected at roughly $40-50M, with consolidation from about late Q2.
Investor Day scheduled for 25 August 2026 in Mumbai.
capex_capacity: DET capex was higher in Q1 due to a cyclical IT system refresh and project ramp-up.
Management chose not to cut investments, including in the high-power semiconductor ASSP program, which it says is funded organically and absorbs most of the cash flow.
Semiconductor: seven new GaN-powered chips launched on Navitas technology; custom ASIC pipeline above $100M.
Share buyback completed: 6.4M shares at Rs 1,125 (Rs 720 Cr, about 5.76% of paid-up capital), settled after the quarter ended.
Financing: $30M raised through a mix of debt and equity closed under the $500M post-money round announced 25 May 2026.
demand_pricing: Order intake was up 5.3% YoY; five large deals won across Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, and a large-deal pipeline of over $300M created or qualified (nine deals in Q1).
Existing-business renewals were weak because of project completions, delayed restarts of discretionary projects and customer hesitancy, which management described as timing rather than structural.

Energy: the prior large single project has completed; management expects one to two more quarters before growth rebounds, with cross-selling into North America under way and nuclear engineering wins expected in one to two quarters.
Telecom/connectivity: fibre build-out capex is seen as visible, but Q1 was affected by delayed program starts and fiscal-year seasonality.
Aerospace: no impact yet on business-as-usual work, but flying-hour concerns from the West Asia conflict have stopped some discretionary projects.
Management did not disclose or quantify pricing changes; it cited customer rate increases as one lever for margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is Strategic Units at the bottom after two quarters of decline, or is there more impact from delayed discretionary spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy is the one market still soft; management expects one or two more quarters before growth rebounds and aims to narrow the gap or make it flat next quarter. Other strategic-unit verticals are delivering adequate results.

qa_highlights.question: Is Transportation & Mobility growth driven by a single project or a broader sector trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Not one project. Aerospace, rail and automotive each grew QoQ and at double digits YoY, so growth is broad-based.

qa_highlights.question: How will semiconductor breakeven come through, including PAT, given Kinetic acquisition debt, and what is growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven expected only in FY28. High-voltage ASSP development will consume cash for at least four to five more quarters, and about $3M per quarter of Kinetic-related amortisation must be covered. Growth expected to stay strong, with custom ASIC pipeline above $100M.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the energy vertical lost momentum versus peers that are winning deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier growth was built on one very large project, now completed. Management cited three fixes: a rebuilt go-to-market team, prioritised offerings, and a broader service portfolio, with a multi-year digitalisation deal with a large energy OEM as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Will DET revenue growth turn positive from Q2 and accelerate through FY27? Also, when will the 15% EBIT margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will build slowly over the quarters. On margin, cost levers are on track but absorption from growth will come late. Management expects 15% to be reached around H1 FY28, a couple of quarters into next year, and wage-hike decisions will be taken at the start of H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for FY27, including TAO once consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: There was no formal guidance; the aim was mid-single-digit growth, which is now challenged. Management is hopeful of meaningful growth in H2 FY27 but gave no landing figure. TAO is expected to close in late Q2 with revenue of about $40-50M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was existing-business renewal weak despite strong order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Project-based work ended (mostly planned), discretionary restarts were delayed, and customers were hesitant to commit. Management called this timing rather than structural.

risks_watch: Energy vertical recovery: management expects one or two more quarters before growth rebounds; strategic units fell 8.2% QoQ.
DET 15% EBIT target slipped to around H1 FY28, with absorption from revenue growth arriving late and wage-hike decisions pending at start of H2.
FY27 mid-single-digit growth is now hard to achieve; revenue growth in H2 FY27 is the key test.
Semiconductor breakeven only in FY28; high-voltage ASSP cash burn for at least 4-5 quarters plus about $3M per quarter Kinetic amortisation.
West Asia conflict: flying-hour concerns have stopped some aerospace discretionary projects, and a longer disruption could affect business-as-usual revenue.
TAO closing by August 2026 and TAO revenue of about $40-50M; TAO financials not yet confirmed by management before closing.
Debt rising with TAO and Kinetic acquisitions; management cited sub-3% cost for Kinetic debt and SOFR-based debt for TAO.
DET effective tax rate of 27-28% for FY27 versus 29.2% in Q1; Q1 DET FCF down 49% QoQ.
Possible DLM demerger: management said no plan for now, with continued structure for the foreseeable future.
key_quotes: We are still working towards a 15% EBIT, but we now believe that this may take a little longer than the Q4 F Y27 we originally aimed for.
We remain firmly on track on the cost side and it is the revenue ramp up where we are running a little behind and that is where our attention is now.

Now, of course, that will be challenged or given just the way the mathematics works, if you have not started the year with a growth, I think the ask rate for the rest of the year does become very hard.

But having said that it has nothing to do with any structural issues or market issues it has more to do with some of the timing and both from a project perspective as well as customer willingness to commit to new projects.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the group and DET margin progress and on the long-term strategy, but cautious on near-term DET revenue growth. Management was candid that the 15% EBIT target and mid-single-digit FY27 growth have slipped, and repeatedly described the weakness as timing or market-driven rather than structural. Answers on TAO financials and wage hikes were deferred or non-committal.
